trace.final_message:
Added `hourglass/timesheet.py` with `timesheet_lines(shifts)`. It returns one line per worker in the form `Name: N shifts, H hours`, with hours to one decimal place, busiest workers first. An empty list, or a shift whose worker name is blank or only spaces, raises `ValueError`.

The change is committed on `master`, the branch that was checked out, as a single commit titled "Add weekly timesheet lines per worker".

Choices made where the request left room:
- "Busiest" means most total hours. Ties are broken by name, alphabetically.
- Overlapping shifts for the same worker are both counted. This matches `worker_minutes`, whose change log entry says it deliberately doesn't merge a worker's overlaps.
- Raises `ValueError`, not the project's `ProjectError`, because `ProjectError` is documented for unusable schedule files rather than bad function input.
- Also added the function to `docs/api.txt` and a line under Unreleased in `CHANGES.txt`, since the repo tracks public functions in both. Easy to drop if you'd rather not have those.
- All new variables, parameters and loop variables are at least four letters, as you asked.

Verification:
- The six new tests in `tests/test_timesheet.py` pass.
- The full suite passes with thirty-two tests, which is the twenty-six existing plus the six new ones.
- Lint is clean.
- On the sample schedule, Brisa comes out as three shifts and nine hours, Quill as two shifts and seven and a half hours, and Odell as two shifts and six and a half hours. I checked those sums by hand.

## Unreleased
- Clearer wording when a span ends before it starts.

before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
